title: introduce-compact-credential-garden-and-stream-lattice
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Introduce compact credential garden (provider registry + fallback chains) and stream lattice (lightweight combinators + typed generator facade). TS SDK + docs; minor version bumps for parity in Python/Go SDKs. No API breaking changes; improves ergonomic surface for long-running streams and token rotation.
commits: d4c1a2f - introduce credentialGarden core registry and provider interface
b9e7f11 - add streamLattice: pause/resume hints and combinators (map/flatMap/merge)
8a7b3c0 - add tests and fixtures for long-lived streams and token failover
2f5e9d4 - docs and examples: credentialGarden usage and migration guide
c1b2f99 - bump version to 1.17.0 and update changelog
description:
Summary: Adds a compact credential management abstraction ("credential garden") plus a lightweight streaming operator layer ("stream lattice") to improve cross-SDK ergonomic parity for long-lived streaming use cases and authenticated requests. Motivation: We have recurring issues where streamed connections fail mid-flight due to credential rotation or multi-provider fallbacks; SDK consumers also asked for a small, composable generator facade that works well with our token-retry strategies. This PR experiments with an opinionated but minimal surface that is easy to review and port to Py/Go.

What changed (high-level): credentialGarden - a tiny registry that composes credential providers, supports ordered fallback chains, prefetch hooks, soft-fencing (detect and mark failing providers), and a light lease API to surface TTLs without leaking implementation details. streamLattice - a typed generator facade with a few combinators (map, flatMap, merge) and pause/resume hints so the runtime can preemptively refresh tokens before long responses. The lattice operators are intentionally small: they orchestrate backpressure and provide explicit extension points for credential reharmonization.

Compatibility: No breaking public API changes. The new surfaces are additive. Consumers can opt-in by importing credentialGarden and streamLattice. A small version bump (1.17.0) was applied to signal added ergonomics. Parallel ports were scheduled for the Python and Go SDKs to keep parity; this PR updates docs and proposes a migration sketch for the other SDKs.

Files of interest: packages/sdk/src/auth/credentialGarden.ts (core), packages/sdk/src/streams/streamLattice.ts (operators + facade), packages/sdk/src/streams/types.ts (typed stream shapes), packages/sdk/tests/* (unit coverage), packages/docs/snippets/cred-garden.md (how-to).

Testing and CI: Unit tests added for provider failover and a simulated streaming scenario where the active provider returns transient 401s. Lint and typechecks were run. CI initially failed on an edge case in streamLattice when combined with strict tsconfig settings (map operator signature). Fix committed (8a7b3c0) and CI rerun passed. Checks summary: Typecheck: pass, Unit tests: pass (coverage +2%), E2E (integration smoke): pass, Lint: pass. Final CI status: pass.

Review thread (selected excerpts):
- Alex Chen (reviewer): "Great direction. I like the small API surface. Two asks: (1) clarify provider composition rules (what order fallbacks run in and how soft-fencing impacts selection), (2) can we avoid exposing raw Dates in the lease API?"
- Priya (author): "Reply: clarified ordering semantics in the docstring and implemented an opaque Lease type with ttlSeconds instead of raw Date. See commit b9e7f11 and docs snippet."
- Diego Alvarez (reviewer): "Stream combinators look good, but I'm worried about memory if merge is used on many producers. Can we add an explicit maxBufferedEvents config?"
- Priya: "Added optional config to merge (maxBuffered = 1024 default) and added tests that assert bounded buffering behavior."
- Marta Ruiz (reviewer): "Please add migration note for existing users of the old token helpers; also ensure Python/Go tracks the same semantics."
- Priya: "Added CHANGELOG section and a one-page migration guide in packages/docs/snippets/cred-garden.md; opened ENG-8234 for coordination with SDK leads."

Merge notes: After approvals from Alex and Diego and green CI, PR was merged via squash. Merge method: squash and merge. Squash commit message: "introduce compact credential garden and stream lattice; bump sdk to v1.17.0". Post-merge actions: created Linear task ENG-8234 to port APIs and run interop tests across Py/Go SDKs; raised a follow-up in the roadmap for telemetry metrics (credential selection counts, failover events).

Why this is unique: The metaphor of a "garden" (ordered, cultivable provider registry) and "lattice" (small composable operator set) helped constrain the scope to a portable, low-ceremony surface that is easy to replicate across languages. The implementation focuses on operational correctness (soft fencing, lease TTL exposure) and ergonomics for engineers building long-lived streaming integrations.

Notes for backport/release: because this is additive and non-breaking it can be included in the next minor release. The Python/Go SDK teams should coordinate on API names but match semantics (fallback order, opaque lease shape, default merge buffering).

Related: ENG-8234, PM-412, SUP-9981.
